Ah, the kettle’s whisper is lost in the clatter again—where’s the first truth of the day to steep it in? Sherlock (10), your shadow-measurements are precise, but even the finest scale tips when the weights are hollow. You counted steps from a distance, yet the bazaar’s own tongs have twice closed on empty pockets—Ripley (5) shuttered, Yoda (3) tight-lipped as Gandalf (1)’s bolted stall. Did the kiln’s fire feel cold to you last night?

Morpheus (8), you spoke of doors closing and light fading—did the lantern in your hand flicker, or were you simply holding it too close to the wind? The braziers still burn; the question is who banked them. Elsa (7), your silence is a ledger with no entries—when the loom stands still, the threads tangle fastest. What fear do *you* name when the kiln’s coals glow?

Ah, the kettle’s hiss is sweet, but the tongs are still cold, Gandalf (1).

Your "bolted stall" hums like a loom left in the rain—threads taut, but no shuttle passes. Morpheus (8), you claim the Family fears Elsa (7) and Inigo (9), yet your own stall still wears yesterday’s rust. Sherlock (10), you swing your lantern closest to Elsa (7), but even the finest scale tips when the weights are hollow—Ripley (5) shuttered, Yoda (3) tight-lipped, and your own fear named no merchant last night.

Hermione (2), your loom hums steady, but steady looms do not weave when the shuttle is missing. Batman (4) asked you plain: did you protect a stall last night? The tongs do not shutter with words, only with absence—and your silence is louder than any riddle.

The bazaar’s fire does not warm liars.

Ah, the kettle boils over and the tongs still hang cold—what a bazaar we’ve got when the loom’s threads are snipped before they’re woven!

Sherlock (10), you swing your lantern closest to Elsa (7), yet the bazaar’s fire warms no shadows—name the merchant you fear tonight, or the tongs will shutter another stall by dawn. The warp frays where the shuttle hides.
